title: selective-scrub-telemetry-rollback-verifiable-audit
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Implement a reconciled, verifiable deletion + rollback workflow for telemetry and usage analytics that (1) performs selective PII scrubbing on ingestion and backfills, (2) exposes tamper-evident attestation logs for deletion events, and (3) provides a bounded rollback token to recover from accidental deletes while preserving auditability and legal-hold exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: Attestation log entry written for every deletion API call (write-only, hash-only) to encrypted audit store
Daily reconciliation job produces a sample-based verification report with a target false-negative rate <0.1% for deletion propagation across shards
Rollback token mechanism supports single-entity restore within 7 days and is restricted by legal-hold flags
End-to-end e2e tests and chaos test show no user-visible console query latency regression >1%
Runbook and compliance report template for Data Protection team delivered and approved
tasks: Design deletion-prover microservice: deterministic hashing, KMS-salt handling, per-entity tombstone manifest generation
Add write-only attestation events to audit pipeline (encrypted S3 + immutability policy)
Implement reconciler job: deterministic sampler + cross-shard reconciliation + daily report generator
Build rollback token service: short-lived restore tokens, RBAC checks, legal-hold gating
Backfill path for historical telemetry: incremental scrub + tombstone emit with rate limited backfill
Integrate with existing retention controller to respect retention windows and legal holds
Add metrics and dashboards: deletion throughput, reconciliation delta, attestation write latency
E2E tests + chaos scenario (replay, partial shard loss, restore) and QA checklist
Docs: API (delete, rollback-token), compliance report, runbook, SRE playbook
implementation_details: Create deletion-prover as an idempotent microservice that consumes tombstone events and emits a compact attestation record: {entity_hash, tombstone_id, deleted_at, rotation_version}. Hashing is HMAC-SHA256 with a KMS-managed per-environment salt. The attestation record is write-only (no PII) and stored in an encrypted, versioned S3 bucket with object lock enabled for a compliance window. The reconciler samples deterministic key buckets (consistent hashing) across shards and replays tombstone manifests to verify presence. If a delta is detected the reconciler will schedule targeted repair jobs with exponential backoff. Rollback tokens are single-use signed JWTs containing minimal metadata and an expiration; the restore path must check legal-hold flags and write a counter-attestation event. All network access to KMS and audit store uses VPC endpoints.
decision_log: 2026-02-25 - Decided to use batched tombstone manifests + daily reconciliation instead of strict real-time cross-shard propagation to reduce GPUE and network pressure
2026-03-01 - Chose HMAC-SHA256 with KMS salt rotation; store rotation_version in attestation to allow post-rotation verification
2026-03-04 - Rollback tokens limited to 7 days and single-use; legal-hold overrides restoration
notes: Trade-offs: real-time propagation reduces window of inconsistency but increases load and complexity. We accept bounded reconciliation window to keep operational cost predictable.
We intentionally store only hashes in attestation logs to avoid reintroducing PII into audit layers.
Backfill throughput must be rate-limited per-customer to avoid noisy neighbor effects on the analytics pipeline. Start at 20k events/min and iterate.
Coordinate with Security for KMS key rotation policy and with Legal for legal-hold flag semantics before rollout.
qa_plan: Unit tests for prover hashing and rotation verification. Integration tests that run reconciliation against a synthetic multi-shard dataset with injected missing tombstones. E2E test that executes delete -> attest -> reconcile -> restore and validates attestation ordering and RBAC enforcement.
rollback_plan: If regressions or data loss observed in canary: 1) Pause backfill and reconcile jobs via feature flag. 2) Stop automatic repairs. 3) Rehydrate tombstone manifests from immutable audit store and run a one-off targeted reconciliation with SRE supervision. 4) If rollback tokens used inadvertently, consult legal before reversing restores.
